name: Congenital Abducens Nerve Palsy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Abducens Nerve Palsy

criteria.description: Onset of abducens nerve palsy symptoms present at birth or within the first year of life
Unilateral or bilateral weakness or paralysis of the lateral rectus muscle causing impaired abduction
Exclusion of acquired causes such as trauma, infection, neoplasm, or inflammatory conditions
Presence of congenital esotropia or strabismus associated with abducens nerve dysfunction
Neuroimaging (MRI) showing absence or hypoplasia of the abducens nerve or normal brain structure excluding other pathology

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital onset with lateral rectus muscle weakness and exclusion of acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by neuroimaging to exclude other etiologies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral or bilateral lateral rectus muscle paralysis
Congenital esotropia due to impaired abduction
searchTerms: difficulty moving eyes outward since birth

common.symptomName: Compensatory head turn to maintain binocular vision
Diplopia in older children (if binocular vision present)
Facial asymmetry due to chronic head posture
searchTerms: crooked face due to head posture
jerky eye movements due to crossed eyes

occasional.symptomName: Ptosis associated with congenital cranial dysinnervation syndromes
Facial nerve palsy in syndromic cases
searchTerms: drooping on one side of face
head pain due to compensatory positioning
needing glasses due to vision issues

rare.symptomName: Associated developmental delay in syndromic presentations

searchTerms: scarring or tightening around eye socket
hardening of tissues in eye area

rare.symptomName: Secondary glaucoma due to chronic strabismus
searchTerms: increased eye pressure from eye misalignment
glaucoma caused by chronic eye crossing
eye pressure problems due to strabismus

imaging: MRI showing absence or hypoplasia of the abducens nerve
Normal brain parenchyma excluding mass lesions or demyelination
genetic: Possible association with congenital cranial dysinnervation syndromes (CCDDs)
No specific gene identified for isolated congenital abducens nerve palsy
other: Clinical observation of ocular motility deficits
Orthoptic evaluation confirming lateral rectus dysfunction

distinguishingFeatures: Onset after birth with identifiable cause such as trauma or infection
Limited abduction with globe retraction and narrowing of palpebral fissure on adduction
Absent or hypoplastic abducens nerve with aberrant innervation

redFlags: Sudden onset of abducens nerve palsy indicating possible intracranial pathology
Progressive neurological deficits beyond isolated lateral rectus weakness
Signs of increased intracranial pressure or mass effect
references: Kanski JJ, Bowling B. Clinical Ophthalmology: A Systematic Approach. 8th Edition. Elsevier; 2015.
Orphanet: Congenital Abducens Nerve Palsy. ORPHA:440233.
Kumar S, et al. Congenital sixth nerve palsy: clinical features and management. J AAPOS. 2017;21(1):52-56.
